issue.title: Run lemma 6a(5) on the M = 5 certificate's exported box

milestone.title: G2 · Theorem A(M = 5)
milestone.description: Wire the review's control fixes into the M = 5 certificate, certify lemmas 6a(5) and 6b1, review them independently, and write up Theorem A(M = 5).

issue.body:
**What.** Certify lemma 6a's backward step at M = 5 from the state box the point certificate exported at xi_1 = 0.3.

**Why.** Digest, item 2c; [proof/A_lemmas_M.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/proof/A_lemmas_M.md); the README table says Theorem A(M = 5) needs lemmas 6a(5) and 6b1.

**Acceptance (each can fail).**
- The run on `data/A_M2_6a_M5_1e-10.json` exits 0, and its mutation control exits 1.
- The enclosure is quoted with endpoints rounded outward.
- Raw output goes to a task folder of the raw-data repository (AGENTS.md), and `python3 raw_check.py <folder> PATTERN` passes on it.

**Files.** [solver/proof/data/A_M2_6a_M5_1e-10.json](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/solver/proof/data/A_M2_6a_M5_1e-10.json), [proof/A_lemmas_M.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/proof/A_lemmas_M.md), [PROOF.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/PROOF.md)

started: macm3 (Apple M3, 24 GB), main checkout at dc3b2d0b (origin/main), venv-macm3 (python-flint 0.9.0), 1 thread, nice 10 under caffeinate -i, at 2026-11-08 01:23 UTC. From solver/proof/, the command of the first comment with the venv's python; log, json and .cmd in `I36-macm3/` of the raw-data repository. Stops after 6 h.

Question on the acceptance's "its mutation control exits 1": the first comment gives no control command, and lemma6_jump_M.py's mutations exit 0 when they fail as expected, not 1:
- `--mutate=swap` returns 0 when rho_6a is not < 1 (or the backward integration fails), and 3 if it passes.
- `--mutate=partial` returns 0 when G_slow is not square.
- A plain run returns 0 on rho_6a < 1, and 2 otherwise.

Which control should I run after this, and with which expected exit? I'd suggest `--mutate=partial` with `--load-B` from a `--save-B` of this run, but this run has no `--save-B`, so that would mean changing the command. I run nothing beyond the given command until you say.

**Stopped (macm3): exit 1 after 20 s, lemma 6a(5) not reached.** The command of the first comment, run from solver/proof/ with venv-macm3 (main dc3b2d0b), 01:23:25 to 01:23:45 UTC.

The log in full (one line):
```
lemma S or the flat estimate failed
```
That is lemma6_jump_M.py line 160. The script checks lemma S and the flat estimate (`L6SM.lemma_S_M(M, rp, k, box)` and `flat_estimate_M`, verbose off) before the backward integration and returns 1 when either fails. So there is no rho_6a and no JSON. The box file itself was accepted: M matched, and the certificate's box lies inside x^ ± 1e-6, since the "not inside" message did not print.

**Likely cause, from the notes, not verified by a run.** The command passes no `--rp`, so the script's default r₊ = 0.1 is used (with k 20, hbox 1e-6, xi_a 0.067). proof/A_lemmas_M.md, "Where lemma S closes", gives M = 5 at r₊ 0.1 as **1.186 / 1.183 / 1.354 (fails)** for k = 10 / 20 / 30. Its certified lemma S(5) uses r₊ = 0.08 (R₊ = 0.0064, k 20, contraction ≤ 0.7247), with the flat estimate at the same Z = 0.004489. So `--rp=0.08` looks like the missing argument. I have not run it, since that changes the command.

The mutation-control question in my "started" comment still stands: the script's mutations exit 0 when they fail as expected.

I'm removing "running" and leaving the issue open. If you change the command here, I'll run it.

Main run (the 01:56 comment's command, 01:57:02 to 01:59:32 UTC, wall 150 s, exit 2). The whole log (3 lines, so the last 20 are all of it):

- Lemma S and the flat estimate close as in the notes (0.7247, Lambda 0.4233).

Next (coordinator). The backward integration underflows because the start box at ξ₁ = 0.3 (radius 4.3e-4) comes from the whole certificate box, h = 1e-10. Lemma 6a only needs to hold at the certified zero, so use a sub-box around the same centre that still passes the Krawczyk test (it then contains the unique zero). From solver/proof/, same venv, 1 thread, each to its own log in `I36-macm3/`:

```

python3 -u certify_M2.py export6a --box=data/A_M2_box_M5_1e-10.json --sub=1e-12,1e-20,1e-21 --out=../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/A_M2_6a_M5_sub1e-12.json > ../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/export6a_sub1e-12.log 2>&1
python3 -u lemma6_jump_M.py --M=5 --box=../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/A_M2_6a_M5_sub1e-12.json --rp=0.08 --k=20 --save-B=../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/B_M5_sub1e-12.json --json=../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/lemma6a_M5_sub1e-12.json > ../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I36-macm3/lemma6a_M5_sub1e-12.log 2>&1
```
- If krawczyk does not pass on the sub-box, stop and post its margins.
- If lemma 6a passes (exit 0, ρ₆ₐ < 1), run the control: the same lemma6_jump_M line with `--load-B=.../B_M5_sub1e-12.json --mutate=partial` in place of `--save-B` and `--json`; it must exit 0 by the script's convention.
- If the backward integration underflows again, repeat the three lines with `--sub=1e-14,1e-22,1e-23` (files named sub1e-14) and post both.
Post each exit, ρ₆ₐ, the start box radius it prints, and where any underflow happened.

### Recommended tasks
(macm3, under AGENTS.md's "Recommended tasks go to the coordinator", 9fffdb2; #36 is blocked, so these come before a closing summary.)

**1. The partial control on the stored B of #36**
- **What:** from solver/proof/, `lemma6_jump_M.py --M=5 --box=<raw>/I36-macm3/A_M2_6a_M5_sub1e-14.json --rp=0.08 --k=20 --load-B=<raw>/I36-macm3/B_M5_sub1e-14.json --mutate=partial`, to I36-macm3/lemma6a_M5_partial_sub1e-14.log.
- **Why:** the acceptance's mutation control has not run yet. B_M5_sub1e-14.json exists now, so the control costs seconds and shows that the post-processing's check fires.
- **Acceptance (can fail):** exit 0 with the line "G_slow is ... not square ... [MUTATION partial: failure expected]". Exit 2 or 3, or any other line, fails it.
- **Depends on:** #36's B at de7f17e.

**2. Why G_slow is not proved invertible at sub 1e-14**
- **What:** rerun the sub1e-14 lemma 6a line with `--verbose` (it prints every 20 steps), and once each with LOHNER_ORDER=32 and with a sub-box of 1e-16 (Krawczyk first, as in the 02:18 comment). Tabulate B's max radius, the final state radius, and whether `Gs.inv()` succeeds.
- **Why:** at 1e-14 the backward integration completes, but B's largest radius is 0.335 against a final state radius of 1.06e-05. That suggests the C¹ variational columns, not the state, limit lemma 6a here (AGENTS.md: a C¹ family integration tolerates widths of only about 0.1% of the radius).
- **Acceptance (can fail):** a table over the three runs naming which setting, if any, proves G_slow invertible and gives rho_6a < 1. If none does, the growth of B's radius along xi from the verbose run shows where it widens.
- **Depends on:** #36 (de7f17e).

Coordinator: macm3's two recommended tasks are filed and labelled macm3: #96 (the partial control on the stored B) and #97 (why G_slow is not proved invertible: verbose, Lohner order 32, sub-box 1e-16). #36 stays open and Blocked until one of #97's settings proves lemma 6a.

**Summary (macm3). Lemma 6a(5) holds on the Krawczyk-certified sub-box 1e-18, rho_6a = [0.2309898799 ± 4.42e-13] < 1.** The measurement and the controls are on #103, which is closed.

What ran, for the sub-box `--sub=1e-18,1e-26,1e-27` (half-widths about the centre of `data/A_M2_box_M5_1e-10.json`):

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `certify_M2.py krawczyk` | exit 0, K(X) in int X, margins +1.000 +1.000 +0.980 +0.980 +0.932 +0.932, so the sub-box holds one zero and it is simple |
| `certify_M2.py export6a` | exit 0, state box at xi1 = 0.3, max radius 4.39e-12 |
| `lemma6_jump_M.py --M=5 --rp=0.08 --k=20 --save-B` | exit 0, 534 s, 615 steps, final state radius 1.07e-09, max radius of B 3.24e-05, \|G_slow^-1\| <= 5.92, \|H\| <= 73.0, rho_6a 0.2309898799 ± 4.42e-13 (an arb ball) |
| partial control | exit 0, "G_slow is 13 x 17: not square ... [MUTATION partial: failure expected]" |
| swap control | exit 0, start box radius 3.48e-01, step size underflow, "[MUTATION swap: failure expected]" |
| coords control | exit 2, rho_6a 3.412, caught |

The sub-box 1e-20w (`--sub=1e-20,1e-27,1e-28`) also passes, with rho_6a 0.08801448685 ± 2.00e-12. Exit 0 in the controls means the mutation failed as required, by the script's convention, which the coordinator corrected in this issue.

**What this establishes, and what it does not.**
- The script's statement: if every J_{D,mu}(xi1) = 0 for mu = 1, 3, 5 at xi1 = 0.3, the whole jump vanishes, for every x in the parameter box, given that the state box contains y+(xi1; x) there. Here that box is the sub-box above, whose Krawczyk test passed.
- The acceptance of this issue named `data/A_M2_6a_M5_1e-10.json`, the whole 1e-10 box. That run never passed. The history on this issue is an underflow at xi = 0.2032 on the whole box, an underflow at xi = 0.0885 at sub 1e-12, G_slow not proved invertible at sub 1e-14, and rho_6a 39.22 at sub 1e-16. The claim here is for the 1e-18 sub-box only.
- The code trusted is `lemma6_jump_M.py`, `validated_int.py`, `lemma6_sector_M.py`, `fixed_point_M.py`, `certify_M2.py` and python-flint 0.9.0, run on one machine. No independent review or second implementation yet, #103 recommends a reproduction on win2.
- Lemma 6b1(5), which the README table also lists for Theorem A(M = 5), is not touched.
